items.title: Macron arrives in Malaysia for two-day official visit
items.summary: SEPANG: French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Malaysia today to begin a two-day official visit aimed at further strengthening bilateral relations between the two countries. In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and France amounted to RM17.78 billion (US$4.17 billion). Imports from France totalled RM11.73 billion (US$2.76 billion), comprising mainly transport equipment, machinery and chemicals.

items.title: Anwar demands bold UN overhaul, urges abolition of Security Council veto
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the United Nations (UN) to undertake bolder reforms, including abolishing the veto power, which has long prevented the world body's Security Council from acting fairly and effectively. Emphasising this at the 16th Asean-UN Summit in Manila, the Philippines, Anwar said the current structure of the UN Security Council required a comprehensive overhaul to ensure the UN remained relevant and capable of addressing humanitarian crises and global conflicts without being constrained by the interests of major powers. Anwar said he had also outlined the need to translate the Asean-UN Plan of Action 2026-2030 into tangible outcomes, particularly in green and digital transitions, climate resilience and sustainable development.

items.title: Malaysia, China agree to deepen AI cooperation, technology transfer
items.summary: MANILA: China has agreed to strengthen cooperation with Malaysia and other Asean member states, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI) technology transfer, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Describing the agreement as a positive development, Anwar said AI cooperation was among the key areas discussed with dialogue partners during the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits here. He said the discussions also covered cybersecurity.

items.title: Anwar warns delay in South China Sea CoC talks could invite outside interference
items.summary: MANILA: Delays in finalising the Code of Conduct (CoC) negotiations on the South China Sea could create an opening for external powers to intervene, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. However, he said Asean and China had yet to set a new deadline for concluding negotiations on the code. Anwar said Malaysia wanted the issue resolved through direct negotiations between Asean and China, in line with Asean centrality, rather than allowing the region to become an arena for major-power rivalry.

items.title: Esscom officer alleges police assaulted wife, brought children to station during murder probe
items.summary: TAWAU: An Esscom officer has claimed that he faced pressure during investigations into the murder of e-hailing driver Nurman Bakaratu, including allegations that his wife was assaulted and their three children brought to the Tawau district police headquarters to force him to accept the investigators' version of events. Inspector John Kennedy Anak Sanggah, 47, the 13th plaintiff witness, said in his witness statement that the incident involving his children took place on Feb 6, 2023, while he and his wife, Vivien Fabian, were in remand. John further alleged that his wife had been slapped, beaten and forced to remove her clothes during questioning while in custody.

items.title: Trial opening of US man accused of killing British woman he met on fetish website
items.summary: Dwain Hall, 54, is accused of kidnapping and murdering Sonia Exelby in October 2025 after the two had corresponded over the internet. According to prosecutors, Hall and the 32-year-old Exelby had communicated for about two years using a fetish website called "Motherless.com" and an encrypted application called Sessions. Hall was arrested after attempting to use Exelby's credit card.

items.title: Asean must strengthen military readiness before crises erupt, says Khaled
items.summary: MELAKA: Asean member states must strengthen collective military readiness before crises emerge, amid an increasingly complex and unpredictable regional security landscape. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said no country could consider itself immune to threats beyond its borders, particularly amid growing cyber threats, technological advances and other non-traditional security challenges. Also present were Army chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman, Asean army chiefs and senior military officers.

items.title: Europe's trade walls cannot keep China out as investments soar
items.summary: CHINA doesn't need to clear Europe's trade barriers. The EU trade deficit with China has nearly quadrupled over the past decade, from around 100 billion euros in 2014 to over 370 billion euros last year, or roughly one billion euros a day, according to Eurostat data. Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) appear to be key to China's growth strategy in Europe.

items.title: Bukit Aman probing Malaysian drug syndicate after Thailand seizes 240kg of meth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman is working with Thai authorities to identify a suspected Malaysian drug syndicate following the arrest of five Malaysians and seizure of 240kg of methamphetamine in Thailand last week. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the department, through its Kedah and Perlis teams, was seeking further information from Thailand's Narcotics Suppression Bureau and Royal Thai Police. Two Thai women, aged 24 and 25, were also arrested.

items.title: US blue wave reshapes Asia's winners and losers
items.summary: A RESOUNDING Democratic takeover of Capitol Hill did more than rattle Asian chipmakers. It set off a macro realignment of foreign policy, energy and trade that could create new winners and losers across Asian markets. Cheaper energy could offer relief across Asia.

items.title: NST Leader: Asean must flex its muscle against transnational crime
items.summary: AT the tail end of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila yesterday, the bloc made progress on a slew of collaborations on artificial intelligence, the digital economy and maritime security. However, like in previous years, Asean barely moved the needle on Myanmar's civil conflict, military crackdowns and persecutions, preferring to uphold "constructive and principled engagement", a position that won't settle the humanitarian crisis in the country. About 3.6 million people are displaced inside Myanmar while 1.5 million refugees and asylum seekers, Rohingya in particular, have mostly fled to Malaysia.

items.title: 170 Johor students graduate from Indonesian traditional dance programme
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: About 170 students from five schools in Johor have completed a three-month programme to learn traditional Indonesian dances and graduated at a ceremony today. The students showcased dances representing various Indonesian regions during the graduation ceremony. Indonesian Consul-General Sigit Suryantoro Widiyanto said cultural diplomacy played an important role in strengthening ties between communities beyond formal government and economic relations.

items.title: Dentist fined RM70,000 for employing unregistered worker, allowing dental procedures
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: A dentist was fined RM70,000 by the sessions court here today after being found guilty of two charges of employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner and allowing the person to perform dental procedures at her clinic two years ago. Dr Tong Soo Huan, 38, was charged with employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner under the Dental Act 2018 at a dental clinic in Jalan SS21/1 here at 12.50 pm on May 6, 2024. The inspection found that the staff member was not registered with the Malaysian Dental Council (MDC) as a dental practitioner, while Dr Tong, who was a registered dental practitioner, failed to produce the staff member's annual practising certificate when requested by the enforcement officers.

items.title: No Cabinet reshuffle needed for now, says Anwar
items.summary: MANILA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has dismissed speculation of a Cabinet reshuffle, saying the government remains stable and focused on delivering its policies. He said there was no pressing need for a reshuffle despite discussions following DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke's resignation as transport minister. On Loke's resignation, Anwar said he respected the DAP leader's principled stance, although he had earlier asked him to reconsider.

items.title: Ismail resigns as Negri Sembilan MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Ismail Lasim has resigned as Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar, with Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi receiving a copy of his resignation letter today. BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the letter was addressed to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. In a statement, Zambry said BN respected Ismail's decision and thanked him for his service throughout his tenure as Menteri Besar.

items.title: Melaka, Negri Sembilan victories could strengthen PN-BN cooperation, says Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The recent election victories in Negri Sembilan and Melaka could serve as a catalyst for stronger political cooperation between Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN). Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the outcomes should be leveraged to strengthen mutual understanding, cooperation and public confidence in both coalitions' ability to provide better leadership and governance. The Kubang Kerian member of parliament said the Melaka election results also highlighted the need for PN component parties, including Wawasan Negara, Gerakan and the Malaysian Indian People's Party (MIPP), to strengthen their election machinery.

items.title: Sri Lanka gets FBI help to crack down on online scammers
items.summary: COLOMBO: The FBI will help Sri Lankan law enforcement detect cyber scammers who have shifted illicit operations to the island following a crackdown in Southeast Asian countries, the US embassy said Monday. Police say scam networks have increasingly moved operations to Sri Lanka – an attractive destination owing to its relaxed visa regime and reliable, high-speed internet. "FBI personnel will work with Sri Lankan law enforcement partners on investigative techniques, digital forensics and case development" in a bid to disrupt transnational criminal networks operating out of the South Asian nation, the US embassy in Colombo said in a statement.

items.title: PH MPs challenge Ahmad Maslan to resign over remarks during Budget debate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan (PH) MPs have challenged Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan to resign over remarks he made during a Dewan Rakyat debate today. Port Dickson MP Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said Ahmad's use of the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 committee-stage winding-up session for the Works Ministry to make politically charged remarks was inappropriate for a member of the unity government. Sri Gading MP Aminolhuda Hassan said the Pontian MP's remarks were inappropriate for a deputy minister in the Madani government, who should have taken a more measured approach.

items.title: Malaysia calls for stronger Asean-South Korea cooperation against online scams
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has called for stronger cooperation between Asean and South Korea to combat cross-border crime, particularly online scams. He said the summit also discussed the future direction of dialogue relations and strategic cooperation between Asean and South Korea. South Korea is Asean's fifth-largest trading partner, with trade valued at RM851.76 billion in 2024.

items.title: Man jailed for life over Dublin knife attack that sparked riots
items.summary: DUBLIN: An Algerian-Irish man was jailed for life Monday for attempted murder following a 2023 Dublin knife attack that injured multiple children and sparked rioting and looting. Riad Bouchaker, 52, was found guilty in July of eight charges arising from the attack outside a school in central Dublin on Nov 23, 2023, which left a 5-year-old girl and a woman in her 30s in a critical condition. Childcare worker Leanne Flynn, who intervened to protect the children, suffered serious injuries and underwent emergency surgery.

items.title: Grab drivers in trial pay lower commissions, record higher earnings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Grab drivers participating in a government-backed trial are paying lower commissions and recording higher earnings, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said 170,944 driver-partners had joined the Grab Service Fee proof of concept as at May 31, 2026. The trial recorded an average service fee of 18 per cent and an effective rate of 15 per cent, below the current 20 per cent commission cap.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - November 16, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KLSCAH land premium cut The land premium for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall has been reduced from RM4.67 million to RM1,000 following a change in land status. EPF investment income rises EPF's investment income rose 30 per cent to RM83.32 billion in the first nine months of the year, despite slower growth in the third quarter. NS trainees as disaster volunteers The government is considering deploying former National Service trainees as disaster volunteers, while also reviewing proposals to extend the training period.

items.title: Zetrix offers RM100mil upfront, 6-month instalments to settle RTD arrears
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has offered to pay RM100 million upfront to be reappointed as a Road Transport Department (RTD) revenue collection agent, with the remaining RM214 million in arrears to be settled over six months. He said Zetrix AI, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, submitted the proposal in a letter to the Transport Ministry dated Nov 5. The ministry forwarded the proposal to the Finance Ministry on Nov 10.

items.title: Selangor identifies 56 flood hotspots ahead of Northeast Monsoon
items.summary: Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the two main rivers contributing to overflow in the area were Sungai Damansara and Sungai Buluh. Klang has the highest number of flood hotspots, with 13, followed by Petaling (11), Gombak (10), Hulu Langat (nine), Kuala Selangor (six), Sepang (three), and Kuala Langat and Hulu Selangor with two each. Hulu Langat has the highest number of flood-prone areas at 37, followed by Klang (33), Sepang (32), Kuala Selangor and Gombak (29 each), Petaling (27), Kuala Langat (22), Hulu Selangor (12) and Sabak Bernam (11).

items.title: Anwar welcomes Indonesia's commitment to tackling transboundary haze
items.summary: MANILA: Malaysia and other Asean member states have welcomed Indonesia's commitment to addressing the issue of transboundary haze. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the issue was raised by Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto himself during the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits today. Acknowledging the complexity of the issue, Anwar said he was optimistic that Indonesia's approach would yield positive results.

items.title: Pasir Gudang MP hands over phone as police probe viral poem
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Pasir Gudang Member of Parliament Hassan Abdul Karim gave his statement at Bukit Aman today regarding his poem titled Patik Tak Rela which went viral on social media. He arrived at the police headquarters at 2:50 pm to give his statement to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Classified Criminal Investigation Unit (USJT), with the recording of his statement conducted by the investigating officer starting at 3:00 pm. “I gave my full cooperation and answered nearly 20 questions posed throughout the investigation session,” he said when met by reporters after finishing his statement.

items.title: Dentist fined RM70,000 over use of unregistered staff for dental work
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 16 — A dentist was fined RM70,000 by the Sessions Court here today after being found guilty of two charges of employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner and allowing the person to perform dental procedures at her clinic two years ago. Dr Tong Soo Huan, 38, was charged with employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner under the Dental Act 2018 at a dental clinic in Jalan SS21/1 here at 12.50 pm on May 6, 2024. The inspection found that the staff member was not registered with the Malaysian Dental Council (MDC) as a dental practitioner, while Dr Tong, who was a registered dental practitioner, failed to produce the staff member’s annual practising certificate when requested by the enforcement officers.

items.title: Malaysia's ITU Council seat opens door to early 6G discussions, says Fahmi
items.summary: DOHA: Malaysia's successful bid to retain its seat on the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Council for the 2027-2030 term will give the country greater opportunities to participate in early discussions on sixth-generation (6G) communications technology and the future of global connectivity. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Malaysia's continued membership of the ITU's highest decision-making body would enable the country to play an active role in setting telecommunications standards, managing spectrum and shaping international connectivity policies. He said Malaysia's participation was also important in sharing its experience in developing 5G networks while amplifying the voices of developing countries in global decision-making.

items.title: Ringgit ends mostly higher against major currencies, slips against greenback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended mostly higher against major currencies and Asean peers on Monday but weakened against the greenback as the US interest rate outlook remained hawkish. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar remained well-supported with the US Dollar Index hovering at 103.398 points ahead of the Fed's Federal Open Market Committee meeting in December. The ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.

items.title: Two held as KPDN confiscates 27,000 hair dye products bearing suspected unauthorised halal logo
items.summary: TASEK GELUGOR, Nov 16 — The Penang branch of the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) seized 27,000 bottles of hair dye products worth RM1.08 million suspected of misusing the Malaysian halal logo without a valid Malaysian Halal Certification (SPHM) in a raid on a warehouse in Kampung Selamat here today. "Preliminary investigations found that the products were suspected of displaying the Malaysian halal logo although the company failed to produce valid halal certification documents to substantiate the use of the logo,” he told a media conference at the warehouse here today. He said the company's modus operandi included displaying suspected fake halal certificates in advertisements on social media and e-commerce platforms, as well as engaging popular social media influencers and affiliate agents to convince consumers of the products' halal status.

items.title: [UPDATED] Bukit Aman verifying nationality of suspect killed in Philippines drug bust
items.summary: He said Philippine authorities had shared details of the incident with Malaysian police. "We have been provided with details of the case by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA). According to the Philippine News Agency (PNA), the operation took place at 4.50pm yesterday and involved PDEA agents supported by Philippine police and marines.

items.title: Pos Malaysia Q3 net loss widens despite revenue growth
items.summary: Revenue for the quarter rose 8.3 per cent to RM501.22 million from RM462.77 million, supported by growth across all business segments. Its pre-tax loss narrowed to RM115.4 million from RM116.2 million. The segment's pre-tax loss narrowed to RM29.6 million from RM31.9 million, despite a RM15 million impairment charge on vessels.

items.title: Johor dengue cases surge 159pct, deaths rise to 18
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Johor recorded 13,641 dengue cases and 18 deaths as of yesterday, marking a 159.4 per cent increase in infections and an 80 per cent rise in fatalities compared with the corresponding period last year. State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said 275 cases were reported in Epidemiological Week 45, up 3.4 per cent from 266 cases the previous week. Johor Baru recorded the highest number of cases last week, with 173 or 62.9 per cent of the state total, followed by Kulai with 70 cases (25.5 per cent).

items.title: Malaysia targets leadership role in green energy through local expertise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Malaysia aspires to be more than just a participant in the energy transition landscape, but instead emerge as a leader, technology owner and creator of opportunities in the green energy sector through the development of local expertise, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof. The Energy Transition and Water Transformation minister said energy transition was not just an environmental agenda, but also a catalyst for economic growth that could create high-value employment opportunities and enhance the competitiveness of local industries. Fadillah said this after officiating the Gading Kencana Solar Farm under the Corporate Green Power Programme (CGPP), which was developed through a strategic collaboration between local renewable energy company Gading Kencana Sdn Bhd and global semiconductor company Intel.

items.title: Ministry allocates RM2m for adoption centres as part of stray dog management efforts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) has allocated RM3.362 million to strengthen stray dog management nationwide through financial assistance to local authorities, awareness campaigns and the construction of adoption centres. Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said the allocation included a one-off grant of RM902,471 for local authorities to purchase euthanasia medication and equipment to capture stray dogs. She said the allocation comprised RM58,841 for 28 local authorities in 2021, RM65,630 for 29 in 2022, RM140,000 for 31 in 2025 and RM638,000 for 71 local authorities in 2026.

items.title: PM: Malaysia, Laos to strengthen bilateral cooperation across key sectors
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the matter was discussed during his meeting with his Laotian counterpart, Saleumxay Kommasith, on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit currently taking place in Manila, the Philippines. In a Facebook post today, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said that in addition to congratulating Saleumxay on his appointment as Prime Minister of Laos last month, the meeting also served as a platform to strengthen bilateral ties. Touching on bilateral trade, the Prime Minister noted that total trade between Malaysia and Laos for the January to August period last year increased by 28.7 per cent to US$55.9 million (RM229 million).

items.title: Suspected migrant smuggling agent arrested after armed confrontation in Pasir Mas
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 16 — Two suspected migrant smuggling agents, or tekong darat, fled after approaching General Operations Force (GOF) personnel with a machete and a sickle, prompting the officers to point their firearms at them before giving chase in Kubang Gadong, Pasir Mas yesterday. Southeast Brigade GOF commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the incident occurred at about 8 pm during Ops Taring Delta, when a team conducting surveillance in an oil palm plantation spotted a group of individuals behaving suspiciously. The operation also led to the detention of 12 migrants, comprising eight men and four women aged between 18 and 36, who failed to produce valid travel documents,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Border economic zone study to guide Malaysia-Thailand border development, Dewan Rakyat told
items.summary: Its Deputy Minister Datuk Mohd Shahar Abdullah said this approach avoids duplicating functions with the Northern Corridor Implementation Authority (NCIA), and simultaneously, maximises potential Malaysia-Thailand cross-border trade. He said the government is currently finalising a study on the BEZ development involving four states - Perlis, Kedah, Perak and Kelantan. “This study aims to assess and explore development proposals for the border area with a focus on key strategic border gates.

items.title: Anwar welcomes progress in Malaysia-China ties, eyes stronger economic links
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Malaysia and China are committed to expanding bilateral cooperation across various fields to create more opportunities that will benefit both countries. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was reaffirmed during his meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila. Earlier, Anwar attended the 29th Asean-China Summit, where he delivered Malaysia’s national statement.

items.title: Government approves RM19.05b MRL sukuk programme to finance ECRL project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The government has approved Malaysia Rail Link’s (MRL) fifth sukuk programme worth RM19.05 billion to support the financing of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. "The sukuk under this programme will be issued as a United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) sukuk, in line with the sustainable development goals," he said at the Tokenised Sukuk Initiative Ceremony under MRL's Fifth Sukuk Programme, in collaboration with CIMB Group Holdings Bhd, at the ECRL Gombak Integrated Terminal Station today. Amir Hamzah said the move continues the efforts under MRL's Third and Fourth SDG Sukuk Programmes, further strengthening its commitment to sustainable infrastructure financing.

items.title: Chow welcomes RM84.3m coastal protection projects as erosion affects 51 Penang areas
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 16 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow today welcomed the implementation of seven projects worth RM84.26 million to address risks in coastal areas in the state. According to the ministry, 51 coastal areas in Penang covering 16.3 kilometres were identified as experiencing erosion. “Of these, seven areas covering 5.6 kilometres were classified as Category One, with erosion rates of between 4.7 and 17 metres a year,” he said.

items.title: Court shuts down DNAA bid by trio in Kepong bak kut teh assault case
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 16 — Three men charged with attacking a patron at a bak kut teh restaurant in Kepong will proceed to trial after the Sessions Court today rejected their bid for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA). According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT), the application was filed by Wong Weng Luen, Lai Kae Bin and Wan Ken Fei, whose lawyers argued that the prosecution had yet to provide the documents required for trial preparation. The judge said trial dates would be set next year.

items.title: Two ex-THP Bina senior executives deny CBT-related charges over RM72,000
items.summary: Former THP Bina Sdn Bhd health and safety manager Nasahruddin Ahmad, 56, and former TH Properties Sdn Bhd deputy general manager Tengku Kamarolhisham Tengku Kamaruddin, 55, who also served as THP Bina Sdn Bhd deputy general manager, entered their pleas after the charges were read out before Judge Rosli Ahmad. THP Bina Sdn Bhd is a wholly-owned subsidiary of TH Properties Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Lembaga Tabung Haji, that focuses on construction and project management. He is accused of committing CBT by not handing over the money to THP Bina Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Thunderstorm warning issued for KL, Selangor and much of Malaysia until evening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today issued a thunderstorm warning for several states across Peninsular Malaysia as well as parts of Sabah and Sarawak, with the alert remaining in effect until 6pm. MetMalaysia said thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected in Perlis, Kedah, Penang, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Negri Sembilan, Melaka and Johor. In Perak, the warning covers Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak.

items.title: Malaysia pushes for open, inclusive trade system at Apec leaders’ meeting
items.summary: SHENZHEN (China), Nov 16 — Malaysia wants the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) to continue playing a role in strengthening an open, transparent, inclusive and rules-based multilateral trading system, with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) at its core. Malaysia’s Ambassador to China, Datuk Norman Muhamad, said this has become increasingly important amid global economic uncertainty, which requires more stable international cooperation to ensure continued growth in trade and investment. Malaysia hopes Apec can strengthen trade and financial institutions while ensuring that member economies do not adopt protectionist trade measures that could undermine the global economic recovery, he added.

items.title: Court fines company owner RM100,000 for letting accounts be used to receive illegal funds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — An owner of a machinery maintenance company was fined RM100,000 by the Sessions Court here today for allowing an individual to use his company’s bank accounts to receive RM190,000 in illicit funds last year. Kong was charged with being directly involved in transactions involving RM190,000 belonging to a bank, through the unlawful use of two company accounts belonging to SKD Technology & Service and Akita Machinery & Service at a bank branch along Jalan Klang Lama on Nov 2 and 3, 2025. Deputy Public Prosecutor Shukor Abu Bakar urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence, stressing that the offence involving the misuse of bank accounts was serious and should not be taken lightly, particularly given the amount involved.

items.title: Johor PKR’s Hassan Karim summoned to Bukit Aman over poem probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim is set to be questioned today over a poem titled Patik Tak Rela , which was uploaded to his Facebook account yesterday. The outspoken politician and activist confirmed that federal police had requested him to appear before the Classified Criminal Investigation Unit (USJT) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) at Bukit Aman here at 3pm today. On Saturday, Hassan posted the poem, which touched on what he described as double standards and injustice in Malaysia’s legal system.

items.title: Police investigate after vessel crashes into Lumut waterfront seawall
items.summary: LUMUT, Nov 16 — Police have confirmed an incident involving a large vessel believed to have struck a seawall near a pedestrian walkway at the Esplanade Wing Lumut Waterfront here after videos of the incident went viral on social media this morning. Bernama reported that Manjung district police chief ACP Hasbullah Abd Rahman said police were investigating the incident. Videos circulating on Threads showed the vessel travelling unusually close to the shoreline before colliding with the structure, leaving part of the seawall damaged.

items.title: EV levy among options being considered to speed up charging network rollout, says Miti
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The government is studying various approaches, including the proposed levy on electric vehicles (EVs), to accelerate the development of charging infrastructure towards the targeted 30,000 charging points by 2030, said the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti). He said among the areas requiring attention is the need to expand the capacity of electricity substations, in collaboration with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) to facilitate the development of more EV charging stations. Sim said that up to Sept 30, 2026, a total of 7,341 public EV charging stations had been installed nationwide, comprising 4,992 alternating current (AC) chargers and 2,349 direct current (DC) fast chargers.

items.title: Fresh from Melaka win, Zahid says BN not looking to rush into more elections
items.summary: BAGAN DATUK, Nov 16 — Barisan Nasional (BN) does not want to rush into holding elections in other states despite its positive performance in several state elections, including the Melaka polls on Saturday. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said, however, that the decision had been left to the respective state leaders to assess whether the time was right to hold elections. Mohd Puad reportedly said the proposal followed the success of the BN-Perikatan Nasional (PN) cooperation formula, which helped both coalitions secure significant victories in the 16th Melaka state election on Saturday.

items.title: Missing Penang doctor, 74, found dead after going missing off Tanjung Bungah
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 16 — An elderly man who went missing while windsurfing off Tanjung Bungah here yesterday was found dead this morning. Penang Fire and Rescue Department Assistant Director (Operations and Rescue Division) John Sagun Francis said the body of Dr Khaw Chun Sein, 74, was found washed ashore on rocks near Straits Quay Retail Marina at 9.56am. He said the second day of the search and rescue (SAR) operation began at 9am, covering an area of 94.76 square nautical miles divided into five sea search sectors and one aerial search sector around the victim’s last known location.

items.title: Govt commits RM10.6m to Long Lellang STOLport safety works after fatal Flying Doctor Service crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The government has allocated RM10.615 million to upgrade infrastructure and facilities at the Long Lellang short take-off and landing airport (STOLport) in Sarawak to improve operational safety after a helicopter crashed and caught fire last September. Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the estimated resurfacing costs were RM7.191 million for the runway, RM1.2 million for the aircraft parking apron and RM224,000 for the taxiway, while building a mini batching plant would cost RM2 million. Hasbi said the STOLport would also receive a rapid intervention vehicle (RIV) worth RM1.2 million to improve its emergency response capability.

items.title: Court throws out Mukhriz’s challenge to RM5m tax bill
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 —The High Court here today dismissed Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir’s application to challenge the Inland Revenue Board’s (HASiL) issuance of Notices of Additional Assessment totalling more than RM5 million for the 2017 to 2019 assessment years. Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad ruled that the court accepted the HASiL’s submission that the issues raised should first be determined by the Special Commissioners of Income Tax (SCIT) through the statutory appellate mechanism under the Income Tax Act 1967. Therefore, the court found that this application is an abuse of the court process,” he said.

items.title: No corruption cases linked to illegal crypto mining in Manjung, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) has not recorded any corruption cases involving enforcement officers linked to illegal cryptocurrency mining activities in Manjung, Perak. Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said this was based on police intelligence records, despite allegations that electricity supplies to cryptocurrency mining premises had been illegally reconnected after being disconnected. He said the police viewed allegations of enforcement officers engaging in corrupt practices or abusing their authority seriously, including those involving the illegal reconnection of electricity supplies to cryptocurrency mining operations.

items.title: Court adjourns Negeri Sembilan Exco suit as parties explore settlement
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 16 —The High Court here was informed today that the parties involved in a constitutional suit filed by 10 former state executive council (Exco) members are in discussions to reach an amicable settlement. Counsel Datuk Mohd Hafarizam Harun, representing the 10 Exco members (plaintiffs), informed the court that the latest development followed a letter dated November10 submitted by the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim alongside with the 10 Exco members to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal, Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad. Counsel Datuk Dr Cyrus Das, for the first defendant (the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary), also confirmed that several proposals put forward by the plaintiffs and the Menteri Besar were being considered by the defendants as well as Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

items.title: Selangor moves to curb Bukit Raja flash floods with new pump system
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 16 —- Three high-capacity pumps have been installed near the Bukit Raja interchange in Klang to mitigate the risk of flash floods, which frequently affect the area, the State Assembly was told today. Selangor Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said the immediate measure was expected to help prevent a recurrence of flooding, particularly around the nearby i-City interchange. Izham also said several locations with faulty scupper drains had been identified, with the defects contributing not only to flash floods but also to road damage.

items.title: PAC raises concerns over policy, project continuity after Loke resignation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) today expressed concern over the potential impact of Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s resignation on policy continuity and major infrastructure projects, warning that political leadership transitions must not disrupt governance or delay critical transport initiatives. PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said any political change must not paralyse decision-making processes, slow down Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd’s (MAHB) post-privatisation operational transformation agenda, or derail the implementation schedules of high-impact projects. At the same time, Mas Ermieyati said the bipartisan committee is also concerned about border enforcement at the country's airports, following the ending of Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain’s secondment as Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) chief.

items.title: Teen girl shot in neck near Ranau river, man arrested
items.summary: RANAU, Nov 16 — A 15-year-old girl sustained a severe gunshot wound to her neck in a suspected shooting near Sungai Keliu in Kampung Tinamom at about 8pm on Saturday. Preliminary police investigations revealed that the victim was at the riverside catching fish and frogs with a male companion, who heard a single gunshot while searching for firewood before finding her injured at the riverbank alongside her grandfather. Police arrested a 40-year-old man at a house in Kampung Tinamom at about 1.30pm on Sunday to assist in investigations under Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder.

items.title: Teen charged over Kuching school axe attack, ordered to undergo psychiatric assessment
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 16 — A 16-year-old male student who allegedly attacked a teacher with an axe at a private school here on October 21 has been charged with three offences – carrying a scheduled weapon, causing hurt to the teacher, and possessing explosives without lawful excuse. Magistrate Leona Dominic Mojiliu, however, ordered the student to be sent to Sentosa Hospital under Section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code for psychiatric assessment and fixed Dec 17 for mention. On the second charge, he is accused of voluntarily causing hurt to a 42-year-old female teacher using a small black axe.
